newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE KEEN TO BOW OUT IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE KEEN TO BOW OUT IN STYLE.

text.p: David Campese, the most prolific try-scorer in international history, will finally wave goodbye to test rugby when Australia face Wales at Cardiff Arms Park on Sunday.
Campese won a recall on Friday, ensuring a 101st Wallaby cap, but confirmed it would be his final test appearance in a remarkable career stretching back to 1982.

"It's good to be back in the team...it's been pretty frustrating sitting on the sidelines," he said. "This will definitely be my last international appearance. It's been a tough year but I hope I will be able to bow out in some style."
Only the second player in the world to win a century of caps after French centre Philippe Sella, Campese has scored a record 64 test tries since his debut against New Zealand as a 19-year-old.

Now 34, he has endured a difficult last tour to Europe, failing to make the test team against Scotland and Ireland, but has belatedly recaptured a place on the wing, with Jason Little moving to centre to partner new captain Tim Horan.

Campese could still make one further appearance in a Wallaby jersey in the traditional end-of-tour non-cap game against the Barbarians at Twickenham next weekend and intends to keep playing provincial rugby with New South Wales in next year's Super 12 competition.

But beyond the statistics -- he has held the world try-scoring record since scoring against France in 1987 and also shares the Australian record for tries in a test, scoring four against the United States in 1983 -- he will remain in the memory for his once-trademark 'goose-step' and tendency to rub many of his opponents up the wrong way.

Among others, he has accused South African players of arrogance and England captain Will Carling of "playing like a castrated bull". He also once claimed the only thing people were likely to get playing on the wing for England were chilblains.
Campese, ironically, is just three days older than Welsh fly-half Jonathan Davies, who returns to international rugby union on Sunday eight years after quitting the game for rugby league.
The last time the pair played against each other was in the 1987 World Cup semifinal, the solitary Welsh victory over the Wallabies in the past 15 years.
Welsh chances have been improved by the injury crisis which has dramatically reduced the Walabies' second-row options.
Skipper John Eales suffered a fractured eye socket against Ireland and his partner Warwick Waugh has also been ruled out by a shoulder injury.
It means a first cap for lock David Giffin and a recall for Tim Gavin, who has won almost all his previous 46 caps in the back-row. Pat Howard has also been preferred to David Knox at fly-half.

Wales: 15-Wayne Proctor; 14-Ieuan Evans, 13-Gareth Thomas, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Dafydd James; 10-Jonathan Davies, 9-Rob Howley; 8-Steve Williams, 7-Kingsley Jones, 6-Hemi Taylor, 5-Derwyn Jones, 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-David Young, 2-Jonathan Humphreys, 1-Christian Loader.

Australia: 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Joe Roff, 13-Jason Little, 12-Tim Horan, 11-David Campese; 10-Pat Howard, 9-George Gregan; 8-Michael Brial, 7-David Wilson, 6-Owen Finegan, 5-David Giffin, 4-Tim Gavin, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Dan Crowley.
